planting.note: Plant container or balled shrubs in spring in moist, well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to partial shade; Seneca was selected for an unusually heavy fruit set compared to the species.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to partial shade, giving it room to grow into a large, multi-stemmed small tree over time. Seneca is a selected cultivar of Siebold's viburnum valued for an especially dense, heavy crop of red fruit that matures to glossy black and persists on the plant since birds are slow to eat it, carried in flat clusters above the flowers long after the creamy-white spring blooms fade. Its coarse, deeply veined foliage and strongly tiered branching give it a bold architectural presence that straight species seedlings can lack. Prune only to remove crossing or damaged wood right after flowering, since it blooms on old growth.

common_name: Golden Wayfaringtree Viburnum (Aureum Yellow-Leaved Lantana Viburnum)

planting.note: Plant container or balled-and-burlapped shrubs in late winter or early spring in well-drained soil in partial shade; Aureum holds its brightest gold foliage color out of the hottest afternoon sun.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in partial shade, with protection from intense midday sun, which can scorch its namesake foliage. Aureum is a long-grown golden-leaved sport of wayfaring tree, emerging bright yellow in spring and mellowing to chartreuse-green through summer, offering season-long color contrast against darker shrubs in a mixed border. It carries the same flat clusters of white spring flowers and the species' striking berries, which pass through green, red, and black stages often within the same cluster. Tough and adaptable like the species, it tolerates dry, alkaline soils poorly suited to many other flowering shrubs; prune lightly right after bloom only if shaping is wanted.

common_name: Pohjan Neito Cranberrybush Viburnum (Finnish Seedless Non-Fruiting Snowball-Type Viburnum)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in average, well-drained to moist soil in full sun to partial shade; Pohjan Neito is a sterile-flowered selection that produces no fruit.

directions: Plant in average, well-drained to moist soil in full sun to partial shade; this Finnish-bred selection of European cranberrybush (its name translates roughly as 'Maiden of the North') produces flat clusters of flowers that are entirely sterile, so no berries ever form. Without fruit to weigh down the branches, the plant keeps a tidier, more refined outline through the season, and the lobed, maple-like foliage still turns attractive shades of red and purple in fall. Its reliable cold hardiness and clean habit suit northern gardens where a fruitless flowering shrub is preferred near walkways or patios where dropped berries would be a nuisance. Prune right after flowering only if shaping is needed, since it blooms on old wood.

common_name: Kilimanjaro Sunrise Doublefile Viburnum (Colorful New-Growth Upright Doublefile)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; a European-bred, plant-breeders'-rights-protected doublefile selection sold under the trade name Kilimanjaro Sunrise.

directions: Kilimanjaro Sunrise, protected under European Plant Breeders' Rights as cultivar 'JWW5', keeps the tiered, horizontal branching typical of doublefile viburnum but opens new leaves in shades of burgundy and bronze that mature to deep green as the season progresses, giving the shrub two-toned foliage interest even before the flowers appear. Rows of white lacecap flowers line the branch tops in mid-spring, followed by red fruit that darkens toward black, and fall color turns a strong orange-red. Its upright habit makes it useful as a specimen or screen where space allows the tiered branching to show fully. Prune right after flowering only if needed, since it blooms on old wood.

common_name: Spirit Laurustinus Viburnum (Compact Dense Evergreen Viburnum Tinus)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Spirit stays naturally dense and compact with little pruning needed.

directions: Plant in average, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Spirit is a naturally dwarf, multi-stemmed, tightly branched selection of laurustinus with bronze-red new growth, bred to stay compact without regular shearing. Dusty-pink buds open to flat white flower clusters from winter into early spring, a welcome source of color when little else is blooming, followed by small blue-black fruit. Its dense evergreen foliage and tidy rounded shape make it well suited to low hedging, foundation plantings, and container culture where a full-size laurustinus would quickly outgrow the space. Shear lightly after flowering only if an even tighter form is wanted.
